rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality expanded blastocyst and the provided 3AA grade, but it likely over-interprets image details such as slight herniation, visible nuclei, and a specific extracellular body that may not be reliably discernible from a single static image.
Thoroughly integrates maternal age, BMI, PCOS, ovarian reserve markers, endometrial thickness, first-cycle status, and male factor with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with a clear link from embryo quality and patient factors to prognosis, though some quantitative adjustments and emphasis on alcohol as the dominant modifiable factor are somewhat overstated.

Mostly aligned on single embryo transfer, antagonist use in PCOS, and general prognostic framing, but includes less guideline-supported elements such as ERA after one failed transfer, strong endorsement of PGT-A, and some speculative supplementation recommendations.
Provides clear practical recommendations for transfer management, monitoring, lifestyle changes, and future planning, though a few suggestions are more opinion-based than standard-of-care.
